newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India to hike domestic oil prices by 15 pct a year.
newsitem.headline: India to hike domestic oil prices by 15 pct a year.

text.p: India plans to hike subsidised oil products prices by 15 percent a year until full deregulation in 2000/2001 to bring domestic prices to international level, an official with state-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) said on Monday.
IOC's Director of Finance, Suresh Chand Mathur, said this was part of the Indian government's "soft landing approach" to deregulating the country's oil sector.

"In July, the goverment of India has raised the prices of petroleum products with the objective of bringing these prices near to the international prices," he told an oil refining conference in Singapore.
He said despite the price hike in July, they still fell 15 percent short of international prices.
The new Indian government initially raised gasoline (petrol) prices by 25 percent and prices for diesel, liquid petroleum gas (LPG), paraffin wax and fuel oil by 30 percent.
But nationwide protests and public outcry later forced the government to halve the diesel price increase.

Mathur said raising domestic oil products prices was a sensitive matter, particularly for kerosene which was not affected by the July hikes. Kerosene is consumed by the poorer communities for lighting and heating.

"It is the government's objective that progressively products that are comparatively not that sensitive will be decontrolled. Other products like LPG (liquid petroleum gas) and thereafter diesel, will be the ones which will come to international parity, leaving kerosene," he said.
Current expectations are that it should be possible for kerosene prices to reach international prices by the 2000/2001, he said.
"But if due to certain reasons it is not possible, the petroleum sector will be made free as has been announced, although the goverment may give certain concessions for kerosene," Mathur said.
